parties.name: Labour
parties.summary: Labour proposes a Warm Homes Plan with £6.6 billion investment to upgrade five million homes, aims to mandate financial institutions to align with the 1.5°C Paris Agreement goal, and commits to reversing Conservative changes to the Bank of England's climate mandate.

citations.quote: Labour will invest an extra £6.6 billion over the next parliament, doubling the existing planned government investment, to upgrade five million homes to cut bills for families.

mandating UK-regulated financial institutions ­ including banks, asset managers, pension funds, and insurers ­ and FTSE 100 companies to develop and implement credible transition plans that align with the 1.5°C goal of the Paris Agreement.

parties.name: Conservative
parties.summary: The Conservatives advocate a pragmatic and proportionate path to net zero by 2050, emphasising cutting costs for households and businesses, scaling up nuclear power, and rejecting what they characterise as Labour's top-down approach.

citations.quote: We will cut the cost of tackling climate change for households and business, and deliver net zero by 2050, by: Sticking to our pragmatic, proportionate and realistic approach that eases the burdens on working people.
We reject Labour's dogmatic, top-down approach that will burden households with higher bills.

parties.name: Liberal Democrats
parties.summary: The Liberal Democrats commit to achieving net zero by 2045, propose an emergency Home Energy Upgrade programme, and support British industry through measures including a Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism and a clear stable roadmap to net zero.

citations.quote: Liberal Democrats are committed to cutting greenhouse gas emissions to net zero by 2045 at the latest.
Setting out a clear and stable roadmap to net zero, repairing the damage done by Conservative U-turns and giving businesses the confidence to invest.
